newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads firm amid brisk demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads firm amid brisk demand.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond prices suffered at the hands of U.S. Treasuries amid hints of higher interest rates, but spreads were steadfast suggesting investor demand remained brisk, dealers said.
The marketing of several large new issues also failed to weigh on corporate spreads, even in the busy bank and finance sector, traders said.
In the high-yield market, prices were estimated down 1/4 point on average after U.S. Treasuries made a decisive move lower at mid-morning, according to junk traders.

Bank and finance paper was notable performer with a recent pileup of supply, traders said, including $200 million Bank of Boston debt on Monday and $70 million Key Bank of Oregon and $250 million SunTrust Bank issues on Tuesday.
"If anything things have improved," one trader said late on Tuesday. "Some paper is getting done at very tight levels."

SunTrust Bank's issued $250 million 10-year subordinated A1/A-plus rated notes, for instance were considered rich by some with a yield spread of 48.5 basis points over 10-year Treasury. Similarly rated paper due 2006 was quoted 10 basis points wider, according to traders.

The Bank of Boston debt widened on the bid side after selling at a tight spread on Monday. The 10-year A3/BBB-plus rated notes were quoted at 70 bid, 65 offer near the close compared with the original spread of 65 basis points.
Looking ahead in the sector, players will vie for $1.4 billion offering of five-, 10- and 20-year debt from NationsBank sometime this week, sources said.

Other new issuance on Tuesday featured a 100-year, $100 million A3/BBB-plus bond issue from Anadarko Petroleum, priced at 69 basis points over Treasuries. Whitman Corp set $100 million Baa2/BBB-plus 30-year bonds to yield 7.29 percent.
Elsewhere, Mexico priced a $1.0 billion 20-year global eurobond issue priced to yield 11.51 percent, or 445 basis points over the Treasury curve.

Turning to junk trade, dealers said prices were not showing significant weakness and quoted bonds off 18 to 1/4 point at the close. Flagstar's 11-1/4 percent debt, which fell one and a half points to 63-1/2 bid on Monday, were unchanged in thin midday trade.
Flagstar debt will probably not be able to reverse its negative trend, however, based on the company's highly levered financial position, according to ane high-yield fund manager in New York.
Shopko debt traded up 1/2 point to one point after the company announced favorable earnings, one trader said. The 8-1/2 percent debt was quoted at 84-1/4 to 85 level at the close, the trader said.
Shopko debt was hit earlier this month after the company announced it will merge with junk-rated Phar-Mor in a deal valued at $1.0 billion.
Shopko creditors cringed when the company said it may conduct a stock buyback via a new debt offering.
